findings.passage: But when you look at in practice, the (state) bill, as written in House Bill 1300 was so restrictive on the type of ID that could have been used, that it wouldn’t have even allowed my Senate ID to count as a state ID.
findings.note: Quoted by The Epoch Times (reporter Beth Brelje) while he was a U.S. Senate candidate: on the kinds of ID accepted under House Bill 1300 (2021).

findings.passage: Do I think you could craft a fairer version of a voter ID bill? Probably could. But 1300 just doesn’t do that. Secondly, I think it’s a solution in search of a problem. We don’t have a problem of people showing up in person and impersonating someone else to vote. That just is not really a systemic problem. There’s no evidence that is a systemic problem anywhere.
findings.note: Quoted by The Epoch Times: says a fairer voter ID bill could be written, says HB 1300 is not it, and says in-person impersonation is not a systemic problem.

findings.passage: We have seen efforts to disenfranchise voters by advancing burdensome and duplicative Voter ID requirements before. This is Jim Crow 2.0.
findings.note: Quote credited to him in a 2021 press release on his own site, issued at an event about House Bill 1300 (which includes voter ID and mail-ballot ID rules).

findings.passage: Thoughts and prayers ring hollow to the families of every victim without action behind them. findings.passage: I will offer legislation to restrict the sale and purchase of military grade weapons and accessories.

findings.passage: “Good guys with guns, couldn’t stop a single well-armed individual with a military grade firearm and enough ammunition to endanger countless law enforcement officials”, Senator Street said.

findings.passage: More than a dozen bills on gun reform continue to go ignored in Harrisburg. I’ve reintroduced my bill to ban weapons of war.

findings.passage: “As rates of violence in Philadelphia, Lancaster, Erie, Reading, and Pittsburgh are all rising, it is time we do something about gun violence,” said Senator Sharif Street. “We certainly should pass bills that a number of my colleagues have introduced, but at a minimum we should dramatically increase funding for safe corridor programs, violence prevention programs, youth sports activities, PTSD training and treatment, and crisis intervention workers.”
findings.note: Press conference after a shooting outside his district office; supports colleagues' gun bills and funding for violence prevention.
subjects: general statement on gun safety laws

findings.passage: A nation that elevates the right to unfettered access to firearms above all, even the right to live free from violence, cannot be civilized.
